Two ways into the Garage.

Adopt the framework or hand-place individual artifacts. Both paths use the canonical skill contracts and configuration rules.

PATH A

Use the framework

Install with npm

On macOS or Linux with Node.js 20 or later, install the official npm package:

npm install -g @buildergarage/garage

Run garage version to confirm it’s installed.

Download a prebuilt CLI

Download garage v0.5.1 for macOS, Linux, or Windows on amd64 and arm64. Prebuilt executables do not require Go.

Verify the signed checksum manifest and your archive's checksum before running it; GitHub artifact attestations are also available. Follow release verification and terminal extraction instructions ↗.

Starting with v0.4.0, macOS executables are Developer ID signed and Apple-notarized. The macOS installer packages in this release are also signed, notarized, and stapled. See how Gatekeeper verifies the signature and notarization.

On macOS and Linux, you can also install a verified release with install.sh. macOS also offers signed .pkg installers; Linux offers .deb, .rpm, and a Homebrew cask.

Or build from source

Install the CLI from the verified source revision:

macOS and Linux
git clone https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage.git
cd builder-garage
git checkout f9786648988f2b8be3080ebde7867580b4236342
./install.sh
garage version

Requires Go 1.27.4 to build. The source installer supports macOS and Linux and installs to ~/.local/bin without changing PATH. On Windows, build by hand. If ~/.local/bin is not on PATH, follow the installer's instructions before continuing.

Windows and manual builds →

Configure your project

Run these from your project's root. In a terminal, garage init guides you through human authorities, policies, manuals, and skill targets, then asks for confirmation.

from your project root
garage init
garage config validate
garage skills install
garage skills verify

Declare at least one supported user-scope skill target before installing. Downloading or building the CLI does not install skills; garage skills install separately installs the complete embedded canonical skill set and adopted manuals. It never invokes an agent or advances a workflow.

PATH B

Use individual artifacts

Download a skill ZIP or manual Markdown file from the Library. Preserve each skill's directory structure and follow your harness's skill-location rules.

HarnessCLI-managed user directory
Claude Code~/.claude/skills
Codex~/.codex/skills
Copilot CLI~/.copilot/skills
Cursor~/.cursor/skills

These are the CLI's default user-scope paths. It also honors CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, and COPILOT_HOME; Cursor uses its default path without an override. Project-scope installs are not supported by the CLI. Harness path behavior was confirmed on macOS; Linux and Windows harness behavior remains unconfirmed.

Browse the Library

Hand-placed skills are unmanaged, not standalone executables. Canonical skills use garage config validate when resolving project choices, so those steps still require the CLI on PATH and valid configuration. Manuals apply only when the project adopts them. Read the configuration contract before use.

What exists today

Available: prebuilt CLI archives for macOS, Linux, and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus signed macOS .pkg installers; npm and source installs; 8 reusable engineering skills; 3 technology manuals (provisional); the operating model, review contract, governance, and contribution guides.

The CLI: manages project configuration; records and reads private local workflow history; installs and verifies canonical skills and adopted manuals; reads issue and pull-request workflow status through authenticated gh; serves a read-only local dashboard when garage web is explicitly run; and reports its version. garage update check checks for newer releases on demand without installing them.

Not implemented: workflow execution or agent orchestration, agent configuration, AI-provider connections, plugin loading, remote services, libraries, adapters, or SDKs.
